findings.claim: 'Upload scorecard emit artifact' and 'Attest scorecard emit (OIDC artifact attestation)' steps are gated on steps.build-scorecard-emit.outcome == 'success' but NOT on the outcome of 'Validate scorecard emit against schema', which has no id: field. A schema-validation failure does not prevent upload or attestation of an invalid emit.
findings.evidence: workflow line 1437: 'Validate scorecard emit against schema' step — no id: field present. Lines 1460-1462: 'Upload scorecard emit artifact' uses if: inputs.scorecard-emit && steps.build-scorecard-emit.outcome == 'success'. Lines 1468-1470: 'Attest scorecard emit (OIDC artifact attestation)' uses the identical condition. In GitHub Actions, an explicit if: condition overrides the implicit success() requirement; the condition inputs.scorecard-emit && steps.build-scorecard-emit.outcome == 'success' evaluates to true even when a prior step has failed, as long as build-scorecard-emit itself succeeded. The validate step's exit-code-1 failure does not prevent the condition from being true.
findings.impact: An invalid scorecard-emit.json (one that fails jsonschema.Draft202012Validator.validate()) is uploaded as an artifact and receives an OIDC attestation via actions/attest-build-provenance. The 023C aggregator will receive a Sigstore-attested artifact that fails schema validation, breaking the aggregator invariant that all verified emits are schema-conformant. The attestation chain becomes misleading — 'verified' no longer implies 'schema-valid'.
findings.mitigation: Add id: validate-scorecard-emit to the 'Validate scorecard emit against schema' step. Change the Upload and Attest step conditions from steps.build-scorecard-emit.outcome == 'success' to steps.validate-scorecard-emit.outcome == 'success'. This gates upload/attest on both build AND validate success. Inline fix; no schema or fixture changes needed.

findings.claim: rule_counts[*].denies counts raw deny findings from policy-check-summary.findings[] (verdict='deny'), not effective post-suppression denies. This contradicts the schema description ('effective denies after suppression, post-waiver, post-rule-config'), the schema verdict description ('deny if any effective deny'), and DISPATCH-NOTE AC (vii) which explicitly states deny-with-waiver should produce 'allow verdict'. The deny-with-waiver fixture's expected-scorecard-emit.json cements the wrong semantic.
findings.evidence: workflow lines 1316-1317: 'if verdict == "deny": entry["denies"] += 1' iterates findings[] unconditionally, counting all findings with verdict=deny regardless of waivers_applied. deny-with-waiver/policy-check-summary.json line 8: SCP-R-001 finding has verdict=deny AND appears in waivers_applied (line 17). deny-with-waiver/expected-scorecard-emit.json line 11: denies=1, waived=1 — denies includes the waived finding. Expected verdict=deny (line 8). Schema line 71 denies description: 'Number of effective denies after suppression (post-waiver, post-rule-config).' Schema line 52-54 verdict: 'allow if no effective denies; deny if any effective deny.' DISPATCH-NOTE AC (vii): 'deny-with-waiver (raw deny suppressed by waiver, allow verdict).' All three authoritative sources say: suppressed deny → effective denies=0 → verdict=allow. The expected fixture says deny=1 and verdict=deny, contradicting all three.
findings.impact: (1) The scorecard misrepresents a fully-waived PR as verdict='deny', diverging from the gate's actual verdict ('allow'). This directly violates plan-doc invariant 1: 'the aggregator MUST faithfully report verified emit content' — a divergence between the scorecard verdict and the gate verdict is a reporting failure, not a smoothing artefact. (2) rule_counts.denies over-counts by including waived denies, causing the 023C aggregator to understate waiver effectiveness. (3) The deny-with-waiver fixture is an incorrect acceptance-criterion anchor: it will cause fix-round reviewers to accept the wrong semantic if left unaddressed.
findings.mitigation: Fix the deny counting to use effective denies. Pre-compute the set of waived rule_ids before the findings loop: waived_rule_ids = {w.get('rule_id') for w in waivers_applied if w.get('rule_id')}. In the findings loop, only increment denies when rid not in waived_rule_ids (i.e., the deny is not suppressed by a matching waiver). Update deny-with-waiver/expected-scorecard-emit.json: set denies=0 and verdict='allow'. Also correct DISPATCH-NOTE AC (vii) note for the 'full' fixture — it says 'allow verdict' but full has an unwaived SCP-R-002 deny, so verdict should remain 'deny' regardless of fix. File as TF-023B-001 if deferring.

findings.claim: rule_counts[*].rule_config_disabled is set to true for 'no-manifest-applicable' observability records in policy-check-summary.disabled_rules. These records are injected by the workflow ('Emit SCP-R-003 no-manifest observability record' step) and are NOT .scp/rule-config.yaml disables. The schema description says rule_config_disabled means '.scp/rule-config.yaml has rules.<rule_id>.disable: true'. Additionally, rule_config_aggregate.disabled_rules is derived from the actual rule-config.yaml (separate path), creating a potential inconsistency between the two representations.
findings.evidence: workflow lines 1326-1334: emitter iterates disabled_rules and sets rule_config_disabled=True for every entry without filtering by reason. workflow lines 729-747: 'Emit SCP-R-003 no-manifest observability record' injects {rule_id: 'SCP-R-003', reason: 'no-manifest-applicable', expires_at: '2099-12-31'} into disabled-rules.json. full/policy-check-summary.json line 22: this entry appears in disabled_rules with reason='no-manifest-applicable'. full/expected-scorecard-emit.json line 32: rule_counts.SCP-R-003.rule_config_disabled=true — set from the observability record, not from an actual rule-config.yaml entry. schema line 81-84 rule_config_disabled description: 'True iff .scp/rule-config.yaml has rules.<rule_id>.disable: true for this rule.' The no-manifest-applicable record does not satisfy this condition. No sibling rule-config.yaml exists in tests/scorecard-emit/fixtures/full/ to reconcile rule_config_aggregate.disabled_rules=['SCP-R-003'] with rule_config_disabled=true.
findings.impact: (1) Any adopter without manifest files will have SCP-R-003 marked rule_config_disabled=true even though they never authored a rule-config.yaml entry, misleading estate observers into believing the adopter explicitly disabled a rule. (2) rule_counts.SCP-R-003.rule_config_disabled=true can diverge from rule_config_aggregate.disabled_rules (which is correctly derived from rule-config.yaml and would NOT list SCP-R-003 unless it is actually disabled there) — producing an internally inconsistent emit document. (3) The full fixture's expected rule_config_aggregate.disabled_rules=['SCP-R-003'] cannot be produced by running the Python code against the fixture directory alone (no sibling rule-config.yaml), making the fixture inaccurate as a transformation reference.
findings.mitigation: In the disabled_rules iteration loop, skip entries with reason='no-manifest-applicable': if isinstance(d, dict) and d.get('reason') == 'no-manifest-applicable': continue. Update full/expected-scorecard-emit.json: set rule_counts.SCP-R-003.rule_config_disabled=false and rule_config_aggregate.disabled_rules=[]. File as TF-023B-001 (can be combined with MAJ-002 fix round). Longer-term: consider deriving rule_config_disabled exclusively from the sibling rule-config.yaml (the same source used for rule_config_aggregate) rather than from disabled_rules, eliminating the dual-source inconsistency entirely.

findings.claim: The pytest suite (test_scorecard_emit_schema.py) validates schema conformance of the fixture files but does NOT run the Python heredoc transformation against fixture inputs and verify the output matches expected-scorecard-emit.json. The test docstring claims to validate 'the canonical expected emit shape the workflow's emitter step would produce' — this claim is not implemented by the tests. Transformation bugs (including MAJ-002 and MAJ-003) are not caught by the 9/9 pass.
findings.evidence: test_scorecard_emit_schema.py lines 65-109: all three test functions load and validate JSON files via jsonschema; none execute or import the emitter Python logic. The 'full' fixture's waivers_aggregate.active_count=2 and by_rule_id={SCP-R-001:1,SCP-R-004:1} require a sibling waivers.json with 2 entries. Glob of tests/scorecard-emit/fixtures/** shows only policy-check-summary.json + expected-scorecard-emit.json in each directory — no sibling waivers.json or rule-config.yaml exists. Running the Python code against the full fixture summary alone would produce waivers_aggregate.active_count=0 (no sibling waivers.json), not 2. The 9/9 pass confirms schema conformance only.
findings.impact: The fixture pairs are presented as input→output oracle pairs but the oracle is never exercised. MAJ-002 and MAJ-003 would have been caught by an end-to-end test. Future refactors of the emitter logic can silently change transformation behavior while the 9 schema-conformance tests remain green. The 'empirically confirmed 9/9 pass' note in the review package instruction is accurate but incomplete about what was confirmed.
findings.mitigation: File as TF-023B-002. Proposed fix: extract the Python heredoc logic into a standalone module (e.g. lib/scorecard_emit.py with a build_scorecard_emit(summary, waivers, rule_config, env) function) and add a 4th parametrized test type: test_transformation_produces_expected_output that invokes the function with the fixture inputs and asserts deep-equal against expected-scorecard-emit.json (excluding time-varying fields like emitted_at). Add sibling waivers.json + rule-config.yaml to the 'full' fixture directory to make the expected values reproducible in isolation.

findings.claim: The rule_config_aggregate expiry computation (workflow lines 1402-1409) only handles YYYY-MM-DD format for expires_at. The rule-config.schema.json uses dateOrDateTime which also permits date-time format. A rule-config entry with expires_at in datetime format expiring within 30 days is silently skipped and not counted in rc_expiring_30d.
findings.evidence: workflow line 1403: re.fullmatch(r'[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}', expires_at_str) — only the YYYY-MM-DD branch is implemented; no elif for datetime format. schemas/rule-config.schema.json lines 39-47: expires_at uses $ref dateOrDateTime which allows both format:date and format:date-time. The 'Emit expired-rule-config one-release warning' step (lines 897-951) handles both formats via 'if T in raw' branch. The waivers expiry computation (lines 1363-1370) also handles both formats. The rc_expiring_30d computation is the only site that handles only the date form.
findings.impact: An adopter with a rule-config entry using datetime format expires_at (e.g. '2026-06-01T00:00:00Z') expiring within 30 days would NOT appear in rc_expiring_30d. The scorecard underreports upcoming rule-config review burden. In practice rule-config expires_at is nearly always date-only; the severity is MIN. Asymmetry with the waiver expiry computation is a latent inconsistency.
findings.mitigation: Add datetime handling to the rc_expiring_30d block (mirroring the existing waivers expiry computation): after the YYYY-MM-DD fullmatch block, add an elif branch using datetime.fromisoformat(expires_at_str.replace('Z', '+00:00')) with tzinfo-None guard and ValueError catch. File as TF-023B-003 if deferring to a maintenance pass.

findings.claim: DISPATCH-NOTE AC (vii) says 'full (multiple waivers + rule-config disable, allow verdict)' but the full fixture has SCP-R-002 with an unwaived deny — verdict for full should be 'deny' even with effective-deny semantics (fixing MAJ-002 only affects deny-with-waiver verdict). The DISPATCH-NOTE's 'allow verdict' label for the full fixture is incorrect.
findings.evidence: DISPATCH-NOTE.md line (AC vii): 'full (multiple waivers + rule-config disable, allow verdict)'. full/policy-check-summary.json line 16: SCP-R-002 has verdict=deny with no corresponding entry in waivers_applied (only SCP-R-001 has a waiver). Even after applying MAJ-002's fix (effective denies = raw_findings - waived), SCP-R-002 has effective denies=1 → verdict=deny. full/expected-scorecard-emit.json line 8 correctly shows verdict=deny.
findings.impact: Documentation only — the DISPATCH-NOTE is a review-phase artifact. However it misdescribes the expected behavior for the full fixture, which could confuse a fix-round reviewer checking AC compliance.
findings.mitigation: Correct DISPATCH-NOTE AC (vii) to read: 'full (2 raw denies: SCP-R-001 waived, SCP-R-002 unwaived → deny verdict)'.

findings.claim: Plan-doc §5 emitter shape (lines 112-136) includes a 'signature' field in the jsonc example that is intentionally absent from schemas/scorecard-emit.schema.json (additionalProperties:false at top level). The plan-doc is now stale relative to D-041's OIDC-attestation decision.
findings.evidence: plan-doc line 135: '"signature": "<ed25519 signature over the canonicalised payload above, base64>"'. schemas/scorecard-emit.schema.json line 7: additionalProperties:false — signature field would be rejected. Schema description line 4-5: 'no in-payload signature field — platform-level attestation is the trust anchor (per WP-SCP-023 §5 step 3 + D-042 to be filed at slice 023C)'. D-041 ratification row in DECISIONS.md: 'Verification: GitHub Actions Artifact Attestation (OIDC-based) via actions/attest-build-provenance@v4.1.0'.
findings.impact: Documentation only. A reader of plan-doc §5 expects a signature field in the emitted JSON but the schema rejects it. Future 023C work referencing the plan-doc jsonc block may incorrectly attempt to add a signature field without a schema change.
findings.mitigation: Remove the signature field from the plan-doc §5 jsonc block and add an inline comment explaining that OIDC artifact attestation (actions/attest-build-provenance) is the trust mechanism per D-041/D-042, with no in-payload signature field.

self_reported_concerns: C-COR-MAJ-002 (denies semantic): my analysis is based on three independent authoritative sources all agreeing that suppressed denies should not count as effective denies — the schema description ('effective denies after suppression'), the schema verdict description ('allow if no effective denies'), and DISPATCH-NOTE AC (vii) ('allow verdict' for deny-with-waiver). However, an alternative interpretation is that 'denies' = raw deny count (for observability — 'how many times did a deny-rule fire, including suppressed firings') and the schema description is simply wrong/stale. If the intended semantic is raw denies for observability purposes, the fix is to update the schema description and verdict description — not the code. I am flagging as MAJ because the schema description is the authoritative contract specification and the implementation deviates from it. If the orchestrator resolves this as 'raw denies is correct and the schema description needs updating', the verdict for deny-with-waiver remains 'deny' and the MAJ is downgraded to a schema-doc correction only.

C-COR-MAJ-001 (GitHub Actions if: semantics): my analysis is based on documented GitHub Actions behavior where an explicit if: condition overrides the default success() requirement. If the GitHub Actions runner has added implicit success() semantics to all subsequent steps when any prior step has failed, even with explicit if: conditions, then MAJ-001 would not reproduce. However, the standard behavior is as I described, and the safe path is explicit gating.

actions/attest-build-provenance SHA a2bbfa25375fe432b6a289bc6b6cd05ecd0c4c32 for v4.1.0: I cannot independently verify this SHA-to-tag mapping without web access. The SHA is documented consistently in the workflow comment, D-041 ratification text, and v1.2.0.md release notes. I take the consistency as evidence of correctness but cannot certify the GitHub marketplace mapping.

The 'full' fixture's waivers_aggregate values (active_count=2, by_rule_id={SCP-R-001:1, SCP-R-004:1}) are hand-crafted and schema-valid but cannot be reproduced by running the Python code against the fixture directory alone (no sibling waivers.json). The fixture is a valid schema-conformance oracle but not a valid transformation oracle. This is the core of MIN-001 — the test design chose schema conformance testing over end-to-end transformation testing, which is a reasonable choice for 023B but leaves a gap that 023C integration testing must close.
summary: The 023B scorecard-emit implementation is architecturally sound: the schema shape correctly covers all plan-doc §5 fields, additionalProperties:false is enforced at every level, no waiver content crosses the boundary, the workflow input defaults false, version-manifest.json / DECISIONS.md / VERSIONING.md / STATUS.md are all updated correctly, and the 9-test pytest suite passes. Three MAJ findings require fix before merge: (1) the 'Validate scorecard emit against schema' step has no id: field, so Upload and Attest steps are gated only on build-scorecard-emit success — a validation failure leaves an invalid artifact uploaded and OIDC-attested; (2) rule_counts.denies counts raw deny findings (verdict=deny in summary.findings) rather than effective post-suppression denies, contradicting both the schema description ('effective denies after suppression') and DISPATCH-NOTE AC (vii) ('deny-with-waiver → allow verdict') — the deny-with-waiver fixture's expected verdict should be 'allow', not 'deny'; (3) rule_config_disabled is set to true for 'no-manifest-applicable' observability records in disabled_rules, which are not actual .scp/rule-config.yaml disables, producing semantic inconsistency between rule_counts.rule_config_disabled and rule_config_aggregate.disabled_rules. Two MIN findings cover a missing end-to-end transformation test and a date-format gap in rc_expiring_30d. Two nits cover a stale DISPATCH-NOTE AC description and a stale plan-doc signature field.
